fact: The fire started in a baker's premises (Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane) after midnight on September 2, 1666
The city had no organized fire brigade, relying on hand-operated pumps and bucket chains
source: The Great Fire of London, Adrian Tinniswood (2003)

fact: Lord Mayor Sir Thomas Bloodworth refused to order demolition of houses for firebreaks, reportedly worried about the cost of rebuilding
source: Samuel Pepys' Diary, entry for September 2, 1666

fact: The fire burned for four days (September 2–5, 1666) and destroyed approximately 13,200 houses
source: Museum of London / London Fire factsheet; figure from contemporary surveys

fact: Molten lead from the roof of Old St. Paul's Cathedral ran through the streets during the fire
source: John Evelyn's Diary, entry for September 7, 1666; also referenced in Wikipedia
